name: Baal
overview: Baal was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Jeiel and Maacah. His mention is brief and limited to genealogical records, with no additional notes provided about his life or role. This places him within the broader context of the Benjaminite lineage as recorded in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Baal is a proper name meaning 'master, owner, lord.' It was not given by God but is noted in the biblical record. This meaning reflects a common Semitic term rather than a unique divine title in this instance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Baal as the son of Jeiel, with his mother named Maacah, establishing his immediate family within the tribe of Benjamin. No further familial relationships are documented beyond this parentage.
scriptureSignificance: Baal's significance lies primarily in his inclusion within the genealogical listings of the tribe of Benjamin. His identification as the son of Jeiel and Maacah helps preserve the historical lineage important for understanding the tribal divisions and heritage in Israel. While not a prominent figure in narrative events, his mention contributes to the faithful record-keeping that Scripture maintains.
